page: Google Cloud Platform ct6e-standard-1t is a specialized virtual machine instance within the ct6e family. It features 44 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and is equipped with 176.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A defining characteristic of this instance is the integration of a single Google TPU v6e accelerator, which provides 32 GB of dedicated high-bandwidth memory. This hardware configuration is designed specifically for machine learning workloads, particularly model training and inference tasks that benefit from Google's Tensor Processing Unit architecture rather than traditional GPUs.

Because this instance lacks local storage, all storage requirements must be met using network-attached block storage, which introduces potential network latency and I/O limits. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities, but the absence of advanced CPU instruction flags means that any non-TPU accelerated vector or matrix operations will rely on standard x86_64 execution paths. From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a balanced ratio of host memory to vCPUs alongside specialized TPU acceleration, making it a cost-efficient alternative to larger GPU-based instances for workloads optimized for the TPU compiler.
The ct6e-standard-1t is designed for machine learning inference, medium-scale deep learning model training, and data pipeline processing that feeds directly into TPU-accelerated workflows.
